day_summary: STEP-ASIDE SURVIVES OPTIONS EXPIRY — BTC REFERENCE CLOSE $62,961.99 (−$1,811.31 / −2.80% FROM JULY 30 REFERENCE $64,773.30): THE $9.6B MONTHLY OPTIONS EXPIRY (FAR LARGER THAN YESTERDAY'S DOSSIER ESTIMATED ~$1.2B — THE JULY END-OF-MONTH DERIBIT EXPIRY IS THE LARGEST OF THE CALENDAR) SETTLED AT 08:00 UTC WITH MAX PAIN AT $64,000 AND PUT/CALL RATIO OF 0.28. BTC BRIEFLY CROSSED $65,000 AT 01:00 UTC ($65,411.23 HIGH — DRIVEN BY THE AMAZON AWS +36.7% AFTER-HOURS EUPHORIA) BUT COULD NOT SUSTAIN ABOVE THE REFERENCE-CLOSE THRESHOLD: THE FRAMEWORK'S 20:00 UTC REFERENCE-CLOSE MECHANISM CORRECTLY PREVENTED A PREMATURE RE-ENTRY SIGNAL. THE EXPIRY PIN MECHANICS THEN DOMINATED: OPTIONS MARKET MAKERS MANAGING $9.6B IN NOTIONAL EXPOSURE KEPT PRICE BELOW $64,000 AT SETTLEMENT, AND POST-EXPIRY SELLING (MONTH-END REBALANCING, SYSTEMATIC POSITION TRIMMING FROM MULTI-ASSET FUNDS) PUSHED BTC TO A DAY LOW OF $62,485.17 AT 15:00 UTC BEFORE A PARTIAL RECOVERY TO THE $62,961.99 REFERENCE CLOSE. THE TWO FRAMEWORK CONDITIONS: (1) REFERENCE CLOSE $62,961.99 < $65,000 — ACTIVE, GAP $2,038.01 (WIDENED FROM $226.70 ON JULY 30 TO $2,038.01 TODAY — 9× LARGER); (2) ETF FLOWS NEGATIVE — ACTIVE (LAST 48H NET OUTFLOWS; JULY 2026 MONTHLY INFLOWS ONLY $205M — A RECORD MONTHLY LOW). HOWEVER, BITCOIN PRESERVED ITS JULY 2026 MONTHLY GAIN: +7.4% (FROM ~$58,600 AT JUNE 30 TO TODAY'S $62,962), SURVIVING THE FOMC HAWKISH HOLD, THE COLDCARD SECURITY SCARE, THE DEEPSEEK AI-CHIP NARRATIVE, AND NOW THE $9.6B MONTHLY OPTIONS EXPIRY. THE MACRO DIVERGENCE IS NOTABLE: US EQUITIES BOOMED (S&P 500 +0.91% TO 7,505.66; NASDAQ +1.1%; AMAZON +9%+ ON AWS +36.7%) WHILE BTC SOLD OFF — A DECOUPLING THAT REFLECTS OPTIONS-EXPIRY-SPECIFIC MECHANICS RATHER THAN FUNDAMENTAL DETERIORATION. AUGUST OUTLOOK IS CAUTIOUS: COINDESK REPORTS THE $60,000 PUT IS THE 'TOP TRADE' AMONG AUGUST PROTECTION BUYERS.

The brief intraday touch of $65,411 at 01:00 UTC (which would have been a false re-entry signal if triggered on an intraday basis rather than a reference close) validated the reference-close discipline — the framework did not trigger a premature re-entry on a momentum spike that promptly reversed.

decision.rationale: Framework Condition 1 (reference close > $65,000): NOT MET — $62,961.99 is $2,038.01 below the threshold. The gap has WIDENED from $226.70 (July 30) to $2,038.01 (July 31), a 9× expansion in a single session. The $65,411.23 intraday touch at 01:00 UTC (before the US session opened) was a momentum spike on Amazon AWS euphoria that was immediately reversed by the $9.6B options expiry mechanics — the reference-close framework correctly filtered this out. Framework Condition 2 (positive ETF flows): NOT MET — last 48h net outflows; July 2026 monthly total ETF inflows of only $205M (record monthly low per CoinDesk). Medium conviction: the step-aside rule is clear and both conditions are decisively unmet, but the July monthly gain (+7.4%) preserved through these headwinds suggests underlying demand above $60,000.

extra.label: $9.6B Deribit monthly expiry — 08:00 UTC settlement with max pain $64,000 / put-call 0.28

This decoupling is best explained by options-expiry mechanics (equities don't have the same end-of-month expiry pin effect), month-end BTC rebalancing, and ETF outflows specific to crypto. It does NOT represent a fundamental deterioration in BTC's macro thesis — the Amazon AWS +36.7% and hyperscaler AI capex cycle that drove equities higher will eventually translate to institutional crypto allocation as risk appetite normalizes post-expiry.

analysis:
## Technical analysis

### Session overview — options expiry dominates; BTC reference close $62,961.99

BTC opened the UTC day at $64,775.47 (essentially unchanged from the July 30 reference close of $64,773.30), briefly surged to $65,411.23 at 01:00 UTC on Amazon AWS +36.7% after-hours enthusiasm, then steadily declined through the Deribit expiry (08:00 UTC settlement ~$63,823), accelerated lower to the day low of $62,485.17 at 15:00 UTC, and partially recovered to the 20:00 UTC reference close of $62,961.99.

### The intraday $65,000 cross — false signal correctly filtered

At 01:00 UTC, BTC touched $65,411.23 — above the $65,000 Condition 1 threshold. This was the highest price in the step-aside framework period. However, this price was reached:
1. At 01:00 UTC (not the 20:00 UTC reference-close window)
2. Before the $9.6B Deribit expiry at 08:00 UTC
3. As a momentum spike on Amazon AWS news, not a sustained directional move

The reference-close methodology filtered this correctly. Within 7 hours, BTC had reversed the entire spike and was trading below $64,000. This is the canonical case for why the framework uses a daily reference close rather than intraday highs.

### Volume — elevated on expiry day; but thin on the real-money side

The $9.6B in notional options expiry inflated volume metrics for the session. Post-expiry (after 08:00 UTC), volume was thin — the Crypto.com candlestick data shows sub-100 BTC candles for most of the post-expiry period, with the 14:00 UTC candle (372 BTC) being the largest post-settlement volume as stop-losses hit below $63,270. The day low at 15:00 UTC ($62,485.17) occurred on moderate volume — not a capitulation spike, suggesting support at that level may be tested again before buyers have fully cleared.

### Trend — step-aside framework; below all key thresholds

BTC remains below the $65,000 step-aside threshold and below the 20-day reference-close moving average (approximately $64,200 based on the prior dossier range). The short-term trend is down; the medium-term trend (July +7.4%) is constructive but the expiry-day selloff resets the near-term chart negatively.

### Strongest support — $62,485 (today's intraday low)

The $62,485 level is where buyers stepped in post-expiry. It represents the post-pin 'true price' — the level where demand emerged after options market-maker hedging was unwound. A return to $62,485 tests whether those buyers are committed or were an intraday technical bounce.

### Strongest resistance — $65,000 (framework threshold)

$65,000 has now rejected BTC twice in the framework period: July 30 intraday ($65,186 high at 13:00 UTC per prior dossier) and July 31 (today's $65,411 at 01:00 UTC). Two consecutive intraday rejections at the $65,000 zone create a genuine supply cluster that will require a significant macro catalyst (September FOMC dovish surprise, major ETF inflow data) to clear on a reference-close basis.

### What invalidates the step-aside

A reference close above $65,000 simultaneously with confirmed positive ETF flows ends the step-aside. The gap has widened to $2,038.01 — from 'closest since step-aside activation' yesterday to a level that represents a multi-week resolution timeline barring a dramatic catalyst. The next realistic pathway: August CPI below expectations (est. August 12) causes September FOMC hike odds to fall, ETF inflows recover, and BTC trends toward $65,000 over 2–3 weeks.
